decisions.decision: Capability probe (canCreateSymlink) rather than a process.platform === 'win32' check
decisions.rationale: A blanket Windows skip would silently drop coverage on the machines best placed to provide it. Probing means the 7 symlink tests RUN on windows-latest in CI and skip only on a developer laptop without Developer Mode.

decisions.decision: Fixed the office/convert.test.ts failures in place instead of skipping them
decisions.rationale: sofficeCandidates and convertArgs are pure and are asked about other platforms; the failures were POSIX literals meeting Windows path semantics, not the code being wrong.

decisions.decision: Rewrote the bridge-plugin fake hermes from /bin/sh to Node
decisions.rationale: Paul's call. /bin/sh does not resolve from Node on Windows (ENOENT, verified). The fake is now a generated .mjs invoked with process.execPath.

decisions.decision: Did NOT weaken the package-io symlink security assertion
decisions.rationale: Per standing instruction. The assertion is unchanged and still rejects a symlinked asset. It is gated on the same capability probe, with an everywhere-runnable companion test that exercises the same lstat(...).isFile() guard.

decisions.decision: Recorded event hooks being dead on Windows as a Milestone 1 gap instead of fixing them
decisions.rationale: Paul's call. It is a product defect, not a test defect, and the fix needs a decision about how Windows invokes a hook. Deferring keeps the milestone green and honest.

decisions.decision: C# native helper for Windows quick controls uses a JSON-lines protocol with a fixed-allowlist dispatcher and a FakeAudioController seam
decisions.rationale: An allowlist is the only way to keep the boundary from becoming a general command runner. Default endpoint switching is deliberately excluded because Windows has no documented public API for it; the protocol returns not_supported for audio.default rather than rely on a private IPolicyConfig contract.

decisions.decision: Audio mapping refactored into pure functions (mapWindowsAudioDevice, parseWindowsAudioStatus)
decisions.rationale: Followed the existing parseWifiInterface / parseActivePowerScheme pattern. Pure functions can be unit-tested without spawning the helper, which is what the new windows-controls.test.ts cases do.

decisions.decision: Updated windows.test.ts:64 instead of weakening the C# protocol to make it pass
decisions.rationale: The test was written before the helper landed and assumed a level of stub-completeness the new helper retired. Updating the assertion to recognise all valid protection outcomes (resolve with panel shape OR reject with a not_supported message) follows the standing instruction on pre-existing test failures: do not weaken security, recognise all valid protection outcomes, and add a comment explaining the security model. The explicit not_supported is the safety net that keeps this from becoming a silent default-device switcher.

decisions.decision: windowsControlsExecutable uses only resourcesPath and cwd, never PATH or environment
decisions.rationale: The boundary exists to prevent unrelated executables from being executed. No PATH lookup, no env override.

decisions.decision: Bluetooth radios only, not paired devices
decisions.rationale: Documented limitation. The helper enumerates BluetoothFindFirstRadio/BluetoothGetRadioInfo. Paired-device enumeration would need a Windows-specific surface and is a deferred candidate.

decisions.decision: NSIS arm64 target uses per-arch extraResources subdirectories and a runtime arch dispatch
decisions.rationale: A single NSIS installer can carry one binary per Windows architecture it supports. electron-builder's win.extraResources accepts per-target subdirs; the Electron host picks the matching one at runtime via process.arch. This avoids the historical alternative of shipping two separate installers (one x64, one arm64) which forces a user who upgrades a Surface Pro from x64 to arm64 to uninstall first.

decisions.decision: arm64 helper is cross-compiled from the x64 dev box via dotnet publish -r win-arm64
decisions.rationale: Self-contained PublishSingleFile output, no separate arm64 build agent needed. Verified locally: file(1) reads the produced binary as PE32+ for MS Windows 6.02 (console), ARM64, 82 MB. The .NET 10 SDK produces real ARM64 binaries from an x64 host.

decisions.decision: NSIS installer rebuild on this dev machine is documented as unverified; the per-arch build script, per-arch extraResources, and arch dispatch are individually verified
decisions.rationale: Three dist:win attempts on this PC hung at the electron-builder asar-packing step. The hang reproduces after a manual 'rm -rf release/win-unpacked' + delete of the runtime 'node_modules/ag-psd/.v8-cache' cache (a runtime V8 compiler cache that electron-builder copies into the asar-unpacked staging area, then can't clean).
